descriptions.text: Gate Pass. When one walks about the streets of any town within the Over City, the mindless Swordsman guards tend to get a bit squirrely if you're carrying a corpse with you. When it comes to their black and white view of justice, the rule of law is absolute. Unless you have a gate pass. This letter gets the city guard off your back as long you're not being too overt with your current criminal enterprise. Pass only works within the township in which it was issued.

beats.headline: On GumGum's body
beats.text: GumGum the orc lies dead in an alley with her chest ripped open and no blood, likely the work of three Krasue. Her inventory holds four gold coins and two pieces of paper, and Carl takes both. One is a Gate Pass. Back at the inn he reads it: the Swordsman guards get squirrely about anyone carrying a corpse, unless they have one of these. The paper itself reads that the holder is doing this on the magistrate's orders, signed Magistrate Featherfall. A Get-Out-of-Jail card, Carl calls it.

beats.headline: A corpse for the desk
beats.text: Look at my desk, you fools, says Miss Quill, because there is a dead prostitute on it. The moment they found the body that morning, with a gruesome note scrawled onto her flesh, Carl called a swordsman over, pointed to the corpse, showed the guard the Gate Pass, and took the body into his inventory. He does not know for certain that it does anything. But if the guards have seen him with the body and, in their odd way, endorsed it, tossing it onto her desk should not count as a crime. Hopefully. Without a word, the two guards turn and walk back down the stairs.
